description: This exhibition follows the groundbreaking career of artist and educator Judith F. Baca and the creation of The Great Wall of Los Angeles. Produced with hundreds of youth, artists, and historians through the Social and Public Art Resource Center (SPARC), the mural transformed the Tujunga Wash flood control channel into a sweeping chronicle of often-unspoken histories of historically marginalized people and their struggles for social justice. A Road of Many Colors: Two Films on Oscar Rabin & Valentina Kropivnitskaya
description: Oscar Rabin wanted to paint. In the Soviet Union that made him a dissident. In 1974 Rabin helped organize an open-air show of unofficial art in Moscow. The authorities broke it up with bulldozers and water cannons. Images of the attack went around the world, and within weeks officials had to allow a second outdoor show. Thousands came. Several years later Rabin and his wife, the painter Valentina Kropivnitskaya, were forced into exile, and he was stripped of his Soviet citizenship. They started over in France. A Road of Many Colors tells their story in two documentaries written and directed by Alexander Smoljanski and Evgeny Tsymbal. title: Health is Human
description: Health Is Human brings together leaders across healthcare, philanthropy, business, and community for a candid conversation about what it takes to build communities where everyone can thrive. Our health is shaped by far more than what happens in a doctor’s office. Where we live, learn, work, connect, and belong all influence our wellbeing, yet the systems designed to support us often operate independently of one another. Hosted by Achievable Health, this forum will explore what becomes possible when we design around people, not systems, and bring together the people and organizations that shape our communities. Music/Words LA: Curated by Inna Faliks
description: Music/Words LA continues its second season at the Wende with Bagatelles, Memories, Magical Creatures . Former Los Angeles Poet Laureate Lynne Thompson returns to the Wende to read alongside pianists Inna Faliks and Gabrielle Sipen. Faliks plays Richard Danielpour’s Bagatelles , a suite of childhood memories from her new album. Sipen premieres Five Hebrew Creatures Suite by UCLA composer Yoni Fogelman. The two pianists then share one keyboard for an early four-hand piece by Arnold Schoenberg. Founded by Faliks in New York, Music/Words is a platform for artists working where music and text meet. This Los Angeles residency at the Wende builds each program around close listening and live collaboration. Inna Faliks is Head of Piano and Professor of Piano at the UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music
